AudioFlipper 1.2 plays a ding when you change the volume, so you can hear the new level.

## New

- **Volume ding**: after you change the output volume, AudioFlipper plays the Windows ding (the
  "Default Beep" sound, the same one Windows' own volume slider makes) at the new level, on the
  device you changed. It dings once when you let go of the flyout's slider, and once when you stop
  scrolling, not on every step. Microphone level changes don't ding.
  - Turn it off with **Output → Ding when changing volume** in the right-click menu.
  - It uses the sound from your Windows sound scheme. If the Default Beep is set to (None) there,
    you won't hear it.

## Installing or updating

Download **AudioFlipper.exe** below. If you're updating, exit the running copy (right-click the
widget → **Exit**) and replace your old AudioFlipper.exe with the new one. Your settings are kept.
It's not code-signed, so Windows may show "Windows protected your PC": choose **More info → Run
anyway**.
